title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: CNBC, CNN and NPR report Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on Wed 18 Nov, above the $70 to $78 range, raising $81.3B from an upsized offering of 980 million shares at a fully diluted value of about $1.5T. ANT is due to start trading on Nasdaq today, Thu 19 Nov, after the opening cross; the opening price and the first-day close are still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
next_label: First trade on Nasdaq as ANT
sources: Anthropic, CNBC, CNN, NPR, Reuters, Investing.com, Yahoo Finance

title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress named interim
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: According to CNBC, interim CEO Colette Kress and chair Harvey Jones spoke to staff on Wed 18 Nov, and Kress said annual pay reviews will move from March to December. Motley Fool and Invezz report the shares fell about 2.9% that day despite the Q3 beat; the board has given no timetable for naming a permanent CEO and has said it will not reinstate Huang.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
sources: Nvidia, CNBC, Bloomberg, Motley Fool, Invezz, Yahoo Finance

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: NBC News and Splash247 report that Iran launched drone attacks on US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain on Wed 18 Nov, after the US strike on Qeshm Island. UKMTO reported a tanker hit by a projectile off Khasab, Oman, that evening, and Iran's army said three tankers struck mines east of Hormuz. Bloomberg reports one of three US carriers has left the region; the blockade remains and no ceasefire has been reported.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: NBC News, CBS News, Gulf News, Splash247, Bloomberg, Anadolu, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Yahoo Finance data show Strategy closed down 6.4% at $90.32 on Wed 18 Nov, and Benzinga reports bitcoin fell below $63,000 that day. Stocktwits reports Monness Crespi downgraded the stock to Sell, citing bitcoin weakness and share dilution used to fund STRC buybacks. The MSCI deletion takes effect after the close on 30 Nov; whether other index providers follow is still open.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Benzinga, Yahoo Finance, Stocktwits, The Crypto Times
